question.text: If the 6-month forward rate of USDINR changes from 83.81 to 83.71 due to US interest rate rising from 5% to 5.25%, what trading action should a trader take?

answer.text: Initiate a short position in USDINR futures
Initiate a long position in USDINR futures
Buy both call and put options on USDINR
Do nothing — interest rate changes don't affect futures prices

explanation.text: The Logic: When the USD interest rate rises while the INR rate is unchanged, the interest rate differential narrows and the 6-month USDINR forward rate declines (for example, from 83.8097 to 83.7076). A trader expecting this should initiate a short position in USDINR futures to profit from the price decline. The Trap: Higher US rates lead to a narrower differential, lower forward premium and a lower futures price, which calls for a short position rather than a long position. Note: Conversely, when INR rates rise while US rates are constant, the forward premium widens and the futures price moves up, favoring a long position.
